questions.q: Why does this capstone model the Procurement business process instead of Sales?
options: SSIS Development's and SSRS Development's capstones already built against Sales, and AdventureWorksDW2014 ships no purchasing fact table — Procurement is genuinely unmodeled territory
Procurement is easier than Sales
AdventureWorks2012 has no Sales tables at all
Sales data is confidential and cannot be used in a course
questions.explain: Both sibling courses' capstones used Sales, and AdventureWorksDW2014 itself has no Fact table for purchasing — choosing Procurement means designing a real star schema from scratch instead of reproducing one that already exists elsewhere in this catalog.

questions.q: What are the four steps of the Kimball business process modeling sequence, in order?
options: Choose the business process, declare the grain, identify the dimensions, identify the facts
Identify the facts, choose the business process, declare the grain, identify the dimensions
Declare the grain, choose the business process, identify the facts, identify the dimensions
Build the physical schema, choose the business process, declare the grain, identify the facts
questions.explain: Lesson 5 introduced this sequence; this capstone runs it for real, in this exact order, across Lessons 36-37.

questions.q: Which real AdventureWorks2012 table holds one row per purchase order line item, including how much of that line has actually been received?
options: Purchasing.PurchaseOrderDetail
Purchasing.PurchaseOrderHeader
Purchasing.Vendor
Sales.SalesOrderDetail
questions.explain: Purchasing.PurchaseOrderDetail holds ProductID, OrderQty, UnitPrice, and the ReceivedQty/RejectedQty columns that track a line's progress toward being fully received.

questions.q: Why does the lesson call special attention to PurchaseOrderDetail's ReceivedQty and RejectedQty columns?
options: Because a purchase order line doesn't get placed and sit still — it gets partially received and sometimes rejected over time, which matters for choosing the right fact table type in Lesson 37
Because those columns are about to be removed from the database
Because they are the only two columns in the entire Purchasing schema
Because they have nothing to do with fact table design
questions.explain: A line item that changes over its lifecycle — ordered, then partially received, then fully received or rejected — is exactly the kind of behavior that drives the fact table type decision made in Lesson 37.

questions.q: What does "scoping" the capstone in this lesson accomplish?
options: It writes down the business process, candidate dimensions, candidate facts, and deliverable in advance, so Lesson 39 can check the finished design against it line by line
It permanently fixes every column name before any design work happens
It replaces the need to declare a grain in Lesson 37
It is purely a formality with no later use in the capstone
questions.explain: Just like SSIS Development's Lesson 46 and SSRS Development's Lesson 38 scoped their projects up front, this scope table is what makes Lesson 39's wrap-up a real check rather than a retroactive rationalization.
